name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_CLASS12_CH08_MATCH_Q01 - Production mechanisms of different electromagnetic wave bands

questiontext.text:
Match the entries in List I with the corresponding entries in List II:

List I (Electromagnetic Wave)List II (Production Mechanism)
A. Radio wavesI. Klystron valve or magnetron valve
B. MicrowavesII. Radioactive decay of the atomic nucleus
C. Infrared wavesIII. Rapid acceleration and deceleration of electrons in aerials
D. Gamma raysIV. Vibration of atoms and molecules in hot bodies

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Framework
According to Maxwell's electromagnetic theory and experimental classifications, different bands of the electromagnetic spectrum originate from distinct physical processes depending on the nature of charge acceleration, molecular transitions, or nuclear disintegrations.

Step 2: Analysis for Radio Waves
Radio waves possess long wavelengths exceeding 0.1 m and are produced by the rapid acceleration and deceleration of electrons flowing back and forth in transmitting aerials. Thus, entry A pairs with entry III.

Step 3: Analysis for Microwaves
Microwaves occupy the gigahertz frequency domain and are produced by specialized vacuum electronic oscillator devices such as klystron tubes, magnetrons, or Gunn diodes. Thus, entry B pairs with entry I.

Step 4: Analysis for Infrared Waves
Infrared radiation is emitted through the thermal vibrations and rotations of atoms and molecules in heated matter. Thus, entry C pairs with entry IV.

Step 5: Analysis for Gamma Rays
Gamma rays occupy the highest frequency region of the electromagnetic spectrum and are produced by radioactive transitions within atomic nuclei during nuclear decay. Thus, entry D pairs with entry II.

Step 6: Final Mapping
Combining all individual evaluations yields the complete match: A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_CLASS12_CH08_MATCH_Q02 - Detection methods for various electromagnetic spectrum radiations

questiontext.text:
Match the entries in List I with the corresponding entries in List II:

List I (Electromagnetic Wave)List II (Detection Method)
A. MicrowavesI. Thermopiles or bolometers
B. Infrared wavesII. Point contact diodes
C. Ultraviolet raysIII. Geiger-Müller tubes or ionization chambers
D. X-raysIV. Photocells or photographic film

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Framework
Detection of electromagnetic radiation relies on energy conversion mechanisms appropriate to each frequency range, including semiconductor rectification, thermal resistance variation, photoelectric emission, and gas ionization.

Step 2: Analysis for Microwaves
Microwaves induce high-frequency alternating currents at microwave junctions that are rectified and detected by point contact diodes or crystal detectors. Thus, entry A pairs with entry II.

Step 3: Analysis for Infrared Waves
Infrared waves deliver thermal energy that heats absorber elements, altering electric resistance in bolometers or generating thermoelectric voltages in thermopiles. Thus, entry B pairs with entry I.

Step 4: Analysis for Ultraviolet Rays
Ultraviolet photons possess sufficient quantum energy to release photoelectrons in photocells and chemically reduce silver halide crystals on photographic film. Thus, entry C pairs with entry IV.

Step 5: Analysis for X-rays
High-energy X-ray photons ionize gas atoms, producing electric discharge pulses measurable by Geiger-Müller tubes and ionization chambers. Thus, entry D pairs with entry III.

Step 6: Final Mapping
Combining all individual evaluations yields the complete match: A-II, B-I, C-IV, D-III.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_CLASS12_CH08_MATCH_Q03 - Technological and medical applications of electromagnetic radiations

questiontext.text:
Match the entries in List I with the corresponding entries in List II:

List I (Electromagnetic Radiation)List II (Prominent Application)
A. MicrowavesI. Remote control switches for household electronics
B. Infrared radiationII. LASIK eye surgery and germicidal water purifiers
C. Ultraviolet raysIII. Aircraft navigation radar and speed guns
D. X-raysIV. Medical diagnostic bone imaging and cancer therapy

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Framework
The interaction of electromagnetic waves with matter depends on their photon energy and wavelength, making specific bands ideal for radar reflection, thermal signaling, precise photochemical cutting, or deep penetration.

Step 2: Analysis for Microwaves
Due to their short wavelengths, microwaves can be focused into highly directional beams with low diffraction spread, making them standard for aircraft navigation radar systems and traffic speed guns. Thus, entry A pairs with entry III.

Step 3: Analysis for Infrared Radiation
Infrared radiation emitted by semiconductor light emitting diodes (LEDs) is widely employed for short-range optical wireless transmission in remote control switches for televisions and electronic systems. Thus, entry B pairs with entry I.

Step 4: Analysis for Ultraviolet Rays
Because of their short wavelength, ultraviolet laser beams can be focused with sub-micrometer precision for LASIK eye corneal reshaping, and UV lamps disrupt microbial DNA in water purifiers. Thus, entry C pairs with entry II.

Step 5: Analysis for X-rays
X-rays pass easily through soft tissues but are attenuated by dense bone structures, making them fundamental for medical radiography as well as radiation oncology. Thus, entry D pairs with entry IV.

Step 6: Final Mapping
Combining all individual evaluations yields the complete match: A-III, B-I, C-II, D-IV.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_CLASS12_CH08_MATCH_Q04 - Maxwell fundamental equations and corresponding physical laws

questiontext.text:
Match the entries in List I with the corresponding entries in List II:

List I (Maxwell's Equation)List II (Governing Law / Physical Principle)
A. \(\oint \mathbf{E} \cdot \mathrm{d}\mathbf{A} = \frac{Q}{\varepsilon_0}\)I. Faraday's law of electromagnetic induction
B. \(\oint \mathbf{B} \cdot \mathrm{d}\mathbf{A} = 0\)II. Absence of isolated magnetic monopoles
C. \(\oint \mathbf{E} \cdot \mathrm{d}\mathbf{l} = -\frac{\mathrm{d}\Phi_B}{\mathrm{d}t}\)III. Generalized Ampere-Maxwell law with displacement current
D. \(\oint \mathbf{B} \cdot \mathrm{d}\mathbf{l} = \mu_0 i_c + \mu_0 \varepsilon_0 \frac{\mathrm{d}\Phi_E}{\mathrm{d}t}\)IV. Gauss's law for electrostatics

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Framework
Maxwell's four equations represent the complete synthesis of classical electricity and magnetism, unifying static source relationships, inductive field generation, and magnetic flux continuity.

Step 2: Analysis for Surface Integral of Electric Field
The surface integral \(\oint \mathbf{E} \cdot \mathrm{d}\mathbf{A} = \frac{Q}{\varepsilon_0}\) relates the net outward electric flux through any closed surface to the net enclosed electric charge, which is Gauss's law for electricity. Thus, entry A pairs with entry IV.

Step 3: Analysis for Surface Integral of Magnetic Field
The surface integral \(\oint \mathbf{B} \cdot \mathrm{d}\mathbf{A} = 0\) over any closed surface expresses the experimental reality that magnetic field lines are continuous closed loops without start or end points, meaning magnetic monopoles do not exist. Thus, entry B pairs with entry II.

Step 4: Analysis for Line Integral of Electric Field
The line integral \(\oint \mathbf{E} \cdot \mathrm{d}\mathbf{l} = -\frac{\mathrm{d}\Phi_B}{\mathrm{d}t}\) around a closed contour represents the induced electromotive force generated by a changing magnetic flux, which is Faraday's law of electromagnetic induction. Thus, entry C pairs with entry I.

Step 5: Analysis for Line Integral of Magnetic Field
The line integral \(\oint \mathbf{B} \cdot \mathrm{d}\mathbf{l} = \mu_0 i_c + \mu_0 \varepsilon_0 \frac{\mathrm{d}\Phi_E}{\mathrm{d}t}\) incorporates both physical conduction current and displacement current due to changing electric flux, which is the generalized Ampere-Maxwell law. Thus, entry D pairs with entry III.

Step 6: Final Mapping
Combining all individual evaluations yields the complete match: A-IV, B-II, C-I, D-III.
